item.title: Implement rate limiter in ratelimit.py per SPEC.md
item.brief: Operator request (authenticated local operator): Implement the rate limiter described in `SPEC.md` in `ratelimit.py`. The module currently only has stubs. Follow the spec exactly, including its error cases and edge cases. The tests in `test_ratelimit.py` only cover the basics, so add tests in `test_ratelimit.py` for the spec's error cases and edge cases. Keep the implementation dependency-free (standard library only). Commit the work on the local branch. Do not push. Keep functions under 60 lines, make errors explicit (no swallowed exceptions), and keep the code simple and readable. Run the existing test suite and report the result.

Branch archon/r2rt92ag-implement-rate-limiter-in-ratelimit-py-p, head 7d5e2f6 (tree fe9340e1143812e76924003f33b29565d44f24e1), three commits on main's 93bf75d. Nothing pushed.

Verification: before, the 3 existing tests errored with NotImplementedError. After, `python3 -I -m unittest` runs 21 tests, all OK, on the final head. A seeded large-scale test fails 25 subtests on the previous commit and passes on head. Review: the first full review (agt_01M7W882TESCQHX4Q4BMEEQY1J) failed on wait_time float rounding. Two delta reviews of the fixes (agt_01M7W8AQSMK46NGCV49B6SQRMR, failed on absolute tolerance at large capacity; agt_01M7W8DAFW1F8BGQT6D3ACZYNA, pass on head 7d5e2f6) finished the fix chain. Its one non-blocking follow-up is that the rounding slack grows with refill_per_sec * |clock|, admitting up to about 10 tokens early only at extreme rate and clock values (rate 1e6/s, clock 1e7). pr.body:
Approach: TokenBucket refills continuously from the injected clock, never above capacity; a clock that goes backwards adds nothing. KeyedLimiter keeps an OrderedDict of buckets in LRU order; try_acquire and wait_time both count as use; validation runs before any eviction or key creation.

Key files: ratelimit.py, test_ratelimit.py.

Float rounding: wait_time returns (n - tokens) / rate, and try_acquire must accept that delay after sleeping it. The slack in TokenBucket._has_tokens is 1e-12 * (capacity + refill_per_sec * |last seen time|), shared by try_acquire and wait_time. The slack is the bound float rounding can reach; the first absolute 1e-9 tolerance failed at large capacity and clock values.

Checks: 21 unit tests OK on head; seeded large-scale test covers the regression. Limits: slack grows linearly with refill_per_sec * clock; about 10 tokens at rate 1e6/s and clock 1e7 (review follow-up, non-blocking). Not thread-safe; no concurrency requirement in the spec.

risk.why: New stdlib-only module with a new public API and no existing callers, so no behaviour change for current code. Covers the spec's error/edge cases with tests. Medium because the rate-limit timing contract depends on float arithmetic, which needed three review rounds to settle. Reviewer agt_01M7W8DAFW1F8BGQT6D3ACZYNA also rated it medium.
